title: Injectivity and projective cokernel descend from a principal cover
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M a finitely generated R-module and N a finitely presented R-module. Let f : M -> N be R-linear. Suppose that for each prime ideal p of R there exists s outside p such that the map R_s tensor_R M -> R_s tensor_R N induced by f is injective and its cokernel is projective over R_s. Then f is injective and N / image(f) is projective over R. No flatness or projectivity of M or N is assumed.

source.place: Algebra, Section 10.23 (Tag 00EN), Lemma 10.23.1 (1),(4); Lemma 10.39.18 (Tag 00HT) (2),(5); Lemma 10.78.2 (Tag 00NX) (1) implies (2)

proof.text: Put Q=N/image(f). Since M is generated by finitely many elements, their images generate image(f). Quotienting a finite presentation of N by these finitely many generators adds finitely many relations, hence Q is finitely presented. This is Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective applied to the quotient map, whose kernel is the finitely generated image of f.

source.place: Algebra, Section 10.23 (Tag 00EN), Lemma 10.23.1 (1),(4); Lemma 10.39.18 (Tag 00HT) (2),(5); Lemma 10.78.2 (Tag 00NX) (1) implies (2)

proof.text: If 0 != x belongs to the kernel, its annihilator is a proper ideal. Choose a maximal ideal p containing it. For the supplied s outside p, injectivity of f_s forces x/1=0 in M_s. The localization zero criterion gives s^n x=0 for some n. Thus s^n is in p, and primality puts s in p, a contradiction. This proves injectivity, including the zero-ring case where every unital module is zero.

source.place: Algebra, Section 10.23 (Tag 00EN), Lemma 10.23.1 (1),(4); Lemma 10.39.18 (Tag 00HT) (2),(5); Lemma 10.78.2 (Tag 00NX) (1) implies (2)

proof.text: The quotient Q_s identifies with the cokernel of f_s. Explicitly the map taking t tensor (y mod image(f)) to the class of t tensor y is well defined; its inverse is induced by tensoring the quotient map. Both composites fix pure tensors, hence are identities. In particular Q_s is projective and therefore flat.

source.place: Algebra, Section 10.23 (Tag 00EN), Lemma 10.23.1 (1),(4); Lemma 10.39.18 (Tag 00HT) (2),(5); Lemma 10.78.2 (Tag 00NX) (1) implies (2)

proof.text: Let T be the set of elements s for which f_s is injective with projective cokernel. Every prime omits an element of T, so Ideal.span(T)=R: a proper span would lie in a maximal ideal contradicting that condition. Flatness of Q_s over R_s is equivalent to flatness over R; apply flatness descent on the unit-ideal localization span to Q.

source.place: Algebra, Section 10.23 (Tag 00EN), Lemma 10.23.1 (1),(4); Lemma 10.39.18 (Tag 00HT) (2),(5); Lemma 10.78.2 (Tag 00NX) (1) implies (2)

proof.text: Apply the finitely presented flat module criterion to Q, using its finite presentation from step 1 and flatness from step 4.

source.place: Algebra, Section 10.23 (Tag 00EN), Lemma 10.23.1 (1),(4); Lemma 10.39.18 (Tag 00HT) (2),(5); Lemma 10.78.2 (Tag 00NX) (1) implies (2)

lean.statement:
theorem injective_projective_cokernel_of_principal_cover
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.FinitePresentation R N]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (h : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], ∃ s : R, s ∉ p ∧
      Function.Injective (f.baseChange (Localization.Away s)) ∧
      Module.Projective (Localization.Away s)
        (TensorProduct R (Localization.Away s) N ⧸
          LinearMap.range (f.baseChange (Localization.Away s)))) :
    Function.Injective f ∧ Module.Projective R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range f)

from.place: Single-bottom-differential normalization: descend injectivity and projectivity from the principal neighborhoods supplied by Tag 00O0.
